P1.evidence: Setter handover mentioned but nothing specific reflected back: 'i know you spoke with kim he kind of gave me like a little bit of a head start on you'. The prospect immediately signalled the gap — 'I'm not sure Tim told you the whole story' — which is exactly what a proper read-back prevents. The frame was the rep's standard two-part version: 'i just want to get a good idea of where you're at you know really build out what it is you want to accomplish and then if there's alignment we can talk about the coaching if not that's fine as well'. No 'what's in the way', no 'what you need'. Agreement was sought and given ('Okay. Okay. Cool.'), and the open question ran verbatim: 'What was it that you were hoping that we could potentially help you with, man?'

P2.evidence: The rep consciously opted out of baseline: 'thank you for telling me pretty much everything I needed to know, all the context, it makes my job a lot easier than, like, trying to ask a million different questions, I appreciate it.' That is the phase being deliberately skipped, not missed. Age 38, the entire nutrition history and the whole training history arrived in the prospect's opening seven-minute monologue and earn no credit. Occupation was never asked in 48 minutes despite the ICP screening on it; height, weight, sleep, energy and results from current training were never touched. The one genuine hit is the injury probe, which was good: 'It sounds like a really big thing for you is that you don't want to get injured. It sounds like that's a big worry, right? Why? What's going on, is there something going on in the body?' — that produced the shoulder click, the rotator cuff and the already-injured arm. He then asked what weight the prospect was using. He did not ask how long any of it had been going on.

P3.evidence: No goals phase was run. Not one of the eight checks was attempted. The prospect handed over the deepest available driver unprompted — 'especially I'm reaching 40, I want to be healthy, want to age well, and my wife is 12 years younger than me, so I need to keep up' — and the rep's entire response was 'Yeah, congratulations.' He also volunteered a future-children thread ('I will have kids hopefully one day') which was ignored. There was no 'who else does that impact', no drive through to marriage or legacy, and no reflect-back. This is the most valuable material on the call and it was left on the floor, which is why the price landed as a shock 25 minutes later.

P4.evidence: The prospect described a decade-long failure pattern unprompted — 'I get into it maybe two months into the training, and then I drop out. When I see my body a bit getting better, then I don't find consistency' — and self-diagnosed it as boredom and gym logistics. The rep asked nothing. No 'why do you feel it didn't stick', no 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way', and critically no 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own', on a prospect who has never had a coach and told the rep directly that accountability is what he lacks.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame whatsoever. A 38-year-old with a decade of failed restarts, a younger wife, no kids yet, weight gained and kept since COVID, and an explicit fear of injury is about as loaded a two-year question as this corpus offers, and it was never asked. No test of willingness to settle, no 'why not', no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: A soft temperature check stood in for the belief question: 'How do you feel about the process?' The answer was warm — 'I cannot ask more than that... I think coaching actually gets me to commit more, since there is someone following up. You don't want to disappoint Trevor' — but it was never converted. The all-in question was never asked, and it is the specific question that would have surfaced the price expectation gap before a number was on the table. The rep moved straight to 'i'll kind of walk you through like the next steps and then uh we can talk about the numbers' without a clear yes.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies. Payment was not collected and, worse, the rep refused an inbound request for it: prospect said 'If you can send me the links, or do we have to do it now?' and the rep answered 'Well, we have to be on a call for me to onboard you.' The Trevor onboarding call was described and loosely indicated ('it'd be friday or monday would be your call with trevor') but never booked. No agreement email, no signature on the call, no welcome email, Skool link or onboarding questionnaire instruction. The call ended on an undated WhatsApp promise.

objection_plays.detail: Money trigger at 00:34:06 ('I didn't think it's going to be that high') and again at 00:36:57 ('Yeah, I feel it's too much'). Some of the play ran: a partial isolation — 'What's holding you back? Is it like the money up front, or anything else?' — a value-projection question that got a yes, and the payment-plan move, 'you don't have to do it all up front if you don't want to. We can break it up for you if that's needed.' Everything else was missed. No 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place'. No permission question about an honest financial conversation. Not one of the six financial-picture questions: no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no credit cards, no available credit, no crypto or investments. The rep also handed the prospect a cheaper-provider frame unprompted — 'I'm sure there's somebody who would do it for 2k' — and then descended the price ladder to $4,000 and $1,200 rather than isolating and solving.

Explicit think-about-it at 00:40:08: 'Let me just think about it. So just to check my options.' No move from the play ran. The rep re-listed payment options instead, which invited the prospect to generate his own cheaper options — he asked about three months, then about one month, and the rep priced both.

Timing trigger at 00:45:22 — the purchase was deferred pending whether he could withdraw from an existing monthly financial product. None of the play ran: no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. No deposit was proposed to hold the position while he checked, which was the obvious bridge.

Script gap — clinical fit again, presenting as fear rather than as a stated diagnosis. The prospect disclosed a clicking shoulder, a self-described 'rotated cup', an arm he had already hurt attempting a kettlebell movement, and a recurring sensation that something will snap overhead. The playbook has no clearance gate, so the rep answered a medical question with a technical one — 'That could be form. It likely is going to be form' — and then told a story about another prospect who badly hurt his shoulder switching to kettlebells. The right move does not exist in the script: nobody is instructed to ask whether a clinician has assessed the shoulder before selling overhead ballistic work.

Script gap — price-expectation shock in a non-USD market. The prospect had internally anchored at roughly SAR 8,000 (~$2,000) for six months and encountered $6,000. There is no scripted way to reset an anchor that is three times low, and no guidance on quoting in local currency. The rep conceded ('Sometimes, I guess, it depends, really') and started discounting by term length instead of rebuilding value.

notes: Forty-eight minutes, an unusually open and self-aware prospect, and four of the seven phases never ran — the rep explicitly told him he did not need to ask questions because the monologue had covered it. The consequence is visible: with no goals depth and no consequence frame, $6,000 arrived naked and the rep spent the last twelve minutes discounting. Two hard corrections: ask the all-in question before quoting, and when a prospect says 'send me the links', take the money rather than booking another call.
